That is a second, separate binding.' DECISIONS.md D8 is the decision to STATE the assumption. This is a published, decided trust assumption, not a hole the corpus is unaware of.

(3) IT ADDS NO ADVERSARY AND NO WORSE OUTCOME. The collusion set {SE, sender} and the victim outcome (receiver books value, receives nothing, attacker keeps their own 1 BTC) are identical to B1 / PROTOCOL §5.7's 'Hacked SE + past owner' row — an explicitly accepted irreducible residual. Capital requirement is the same. TRUST-MODEL §3 defines the 'SE' as 'an API server + database + enclave(s)', one trust unit, so the coordinator is inside it.

WHAT GENUINELY SURVIVES, and it is real: D28's own premise is that the coordinator is 'the party the receiver is being protected FROM' and that the enclave is a separate, stronger witness; B1's mitigation column makes the same split ('the enclave narrows it'). Under that split — an attacker with coordinator DB/API control who cannot break the enclave — B1 is unavailable but this attack is. So the decision to leave D8(2)/(3) as a stated assumption is inconsistent with the split the design has already started building, and the fix is cheap.
flaws.corrected_design_fix:
Take the PROOF OF POSSESSION half of the proposed fix; drop the second half.

SOUND AND SUFFICIENT: at claim time the receiver sends a fresh 32-byte nonce ρ; after the keyupdate commits, the enclave signs (domain tag ‖ sid ‖ ρ) with its NEW share e′ and returns (P, σ). The receiver requires σ to verify under P AND o2·G + P == the taproot internal key of F read from the chain. o2 is fresh per transfer and unknown to the sender, so a forger must sign under A_D − O2 with no discrete log. This one check collapses the whole substitution class simultaneously — wrong `aggregate_xonly`, wrong `x1_pub`, wrong `server_public_key`, and rogue-U — and it binds sid to the on-chain key without any new coordinator column being trusted.

DROP AS REDUNDANT: making the aggregate an enclave fact (passing `user_public_key` into `/get_public_key`, folding A into a v3 attestation digest) buys nothing once the PoP exists — the PoP already binds sid ↔ on-chain key ↔ the enclave's live share — while adding a deposit-route change, a new enclave-held value the enclave cannot verify, and a v3 attestation migration. Keep `aggregate_xonly` exactly where it is, as a D27-pattern cross-check.

STATE THE LIMIT: the PoP does not help if the enclave itself is compromised; that case stays B1 and must be said so, or the fix will be over-read.

DOCUMENTATION: add the coordinator row to TRUST-MODEL's B-table. Note TRUST-MODEL is already stale on this page — §3 still says 'there is no client-facing attestation today', which D8-CLOSE has falsified — so the sync is owed regardless.

flaws.title: The attested count and budget are plaintext rows in an operator-administered Postgres — a signature over untrusted state
flaws.goal_threatened: The census's right-hand side, and therefore admission soundness for a receiver or a pre-paying SSP that treats the attestation as authoritative.
flaws.scenario: Confirmed. `sig_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0` / `sig_budget INTEGER` are plain columns (db_manager.cpp:83-87, :119-130); `attest_sig_count` signs a digest the caller assembles from a plain DB read, decrypting only the keypair (enclave.cpp:280-338); the lockbox DB is an operator-run postgres container on a plain volume (docker-compose-lockbox.yml). Production runs lockbox with no SGX (D22), so there is no sealed monotonic state and no rollback resistance. `UPDATE ... SET sig_count = sig_count - 1` absorbs one hidden co-signed rival state and the receiver now holds a VALID signature affirming the wrong number.
flaws.refutation:
SURVIVES, but two of its claims are overstated and the severity comes down.

(1) 'RELOCATED, NOT CLOSED' / 'SURVIVES VERBATIM' IS UNFAIR. Before D8-CLOSE the under-report was an in-flight edit of a JSON integer inside the coordinator process — per-request, targeted, stateless, requiring only application-layer control, leaving nothing behind. After it, the attacker must obtain WRITE access to the SE's own persistent store, the tamper is durable, the coin's count is permanently skewed (every later legitimate co-sign re-increments from the wrong base), and the coordinator process alone can no longer do it. That is a genuine reduction in attack surface and a genuine change in required privilege, not a rename.

(2) THE ADVERSARY ALREADY OWNS AN EQUIVALENT RESIDUAL. The attack needs {operator with lockbox-DB write, colluding current owner}. That is the same collusion set as B1, with the same victim outcome (a receiver books value and can be raced out of it). B1 is accepted as irreducible. So the marginal security loss over what the model already concedes is small — the finding's real weight is that D8(a) is listed as CLOSED when a load-bearing assumption behind it is unstated.

(3) PART (1) OF THE PROPOSED FIX DOES NOT WORK ON ITS OWN. Folding (count, budget, epoch) into the sealed blob does not stop a rollback: an operator who restores the whole ROW from a backup gets the old sealed blob, and the same long-lived seed (enclave.cpp:270-276, one boot-time seed) decrypts it. The finding is right that part (2) — a rollback-resistant monotonic anchor — is the load-bearing half, and right that it is unavailable in the shipping lockbox.

What survives cleanly: the corpus's assumption inventory speaks about enclave BEHAVIOUR (erasure, one-shot secnonce, ratchet direction) and never about enclave STATE INTEGRITY, and that missing assumption is load-bearing for the only theft-class row the corpus records as closed.
flaws.corrected_design_fix:
Mostly a specification correction, plus one cheap detection mechanism that needs no trusted hardware.

(1) SPLIT THE D8(a) CLAIM HONESTLY. Record D8(a) as closing the TRANSPORT half — the coordinator can no longer alter the count in flight, and can no longer substitute the enclave key either (verify_sig_count_attestation cross-checks it against the lockbox's own reply). Record the STATE half as open, with an explicit named assumption beside T-SE-1: 'the operator does not write to, restore, or roll back the SE's persistent counter state.' Say plainly that on lockbox (no SGX, D22) this assumption has the same strength as T-SE-1 itself.

(2) ADD DETECTION, NOT PREVENTION — this is D8's own option (c) and it is buildable today. Have the enclave maintain an append-only hash chain over increments, h_n = H(h_{n-1} ‖ sid ‖ n), and publish h_n inside the attestation digest (a v3 field). Owners record the head they last saw. A rollback then produces a head that no owner holding a prior receipt can match, converting a silent decrement into an attributable, exhibitable one. This costs one column and one hash per co-sign and does not require sealing or SGX.

(3) DO NOT ship sealed-counter-only (proposed part 1) and call it closed — without rollback resistance it changes the attack from one SQL statement to one row restore, which is not a security boundary. If SGX is ever revived, then require a monotonic anchor and fail-closed attestation as normative for any SE claiming D28's property.

flaws.title: The census counts SIGHASHES but accepts only SIGNED TRANSACTIONS as disclosure — one lost co-sign reply permanently bricks a coin
flaws.goal_threatened: Not G8 or G4. Nothing is confiscated and the exit walk is unchanged — the pre-signed tier chain is intact and the value is recoverable unilaterally. What is lost is the coin's COOPERATIVE/off-chain life, which is exactly B10's already-named damage class, extended from one operation to one coin. State it against that, not against the no-confiscation goal.
flaws.scenario: Reachable as described, with two corrections: (a) the deficit does not compound — a later co-sign adds +1 to BOTH sides of the census, so the coin stays exactly one slot short, not two; (b) the leaf is not only un-conveyable, it also poisons descendants, because verify_conveyed_child re-runs the census over every ancestor's num_sigs (tesr.rs:11955), so a split of the bricked leaf is refused too.
flaws.refutation: The window is real and I could not close it: the lockbox cache is keyed on `session_key` (server.cpp:105-115), the session is a function of (aggnonce, msg, keyagg) and the client's own nonce lives only in the local `Coin` binding inside cosign_tier, so the re-serve genuinely cannot survive a process restart. But three of the claim's supports fail. (1) The design already carries the named terminal state the finding says is absent — `SplitStage::Stranded` is documented verbatim as "the irreducible window: the SE consumed the budget but this process never recorded the co-signature ... Recorded — never silently dropped — so the wallet can SAY so instead of looking idle" (tesr.rs:4318-4322), and `split_is_retryable` already consults the SE fail-closed before re-running a Planned record (tesr.rs:5449-5459). The gap is that the renewal and cancel-reclaim lanes do not inherit that discipline, not that the design lacks the concept. (2) The claimed goals are wrong: no funds are at risk, so this is B10's family (cooperative path lost, value exits), not a confiscation or a bounded-exit failure. (3) The proposed 'real fix' — make the disclosure unit the sighash — rests on a FALSE premise and must not be built. The SE never receives the sighash: `PartialSignatureRequestPayload` carries only {statechain_id, negate_seckey, session, signed_statechain_id, server_pub_nonce} (lib/src/transaction.rs:44-50), and `enclave::partial_signature` is handed the serialized MuSig2 session, from which the message is not recoverable. So 'the SE already sees every sighash it signs, so attesting the multiset costs zero blindness' is false; a client-supplied sighash register would be forgeable and would DESTROY the census rather than strengthen it. A session-multiset variant is constructible, but it requires the sender to disclose the per-tier aggnonce and it requires the disclosure-uniqueness check (today keyed on txid — `superseded_dedup`'s "disclosed more than once") to be re-keyed on session, because a deterministic rebuild after exactly this crash produces the IDENTICAL transaction twice. So the finding's own fix (2) does not even repair the finding's own scenario as specified.
flaws.corrected_design_fix: Adopt fix (1) only, and note that the finding is right that it needs no secnonce persistence: `cosign_tier_request` produces partial.client_partial_sig BEFORE sign/second, so the durable record is {sid, encoded_unsigned_tx, msg, encoded_session, client_partial_sig, output_pubkey} and carries no nonce-reuse hazard. Three additions the finding misses. (a) The idempotent re-serve must be normative at EVERY gate in front of it, not only at the lockbox: the coordinator's sign/second re-checks `finalized >= budget` and returns 410 with no cache (server/src/endpoints/sign.rs:293-299), so today a replay of the budget-CONSUMING signature — the one B10 is about — is refused before it ever reaches the lockbox cache, and the in-process [KEYSTONE] retry loop fails there too. (b) Add a census SELF-CHECK at wallet open: fetch the attested (count, budget) per sid and compare against the local bundle's `expected`; report DEGRADED, never idle. The predicate already exists — verify_bundle rejects an undercount as well as an overcount (`rejects_undercount`) — so this is wiring, not new logic. (c) Give the renewal and cancel-reclaim lanes the Stranded state and the pre-flight SE consult that the split lane already has. Reject fix (2).

flaws.title: Residual B10 is parked as irreducible on a premise the protocol itself now falsifies
flaws.goal_threatened: Documentation integrity only. No protocol goal is threatened, and the row does not in fact close the residual as unfixable.
flaws.scenario: The sentence is genuinely false about the specified signing round: the lockbox checks the (statechain_id, session) cache BEFORE the secnonce consume and returns the original partial verbatim, with the budget check placed after it on purpose (server.cpp:105-131), and the client's [KEYSTONE] retry loop rests entirely on that (tesr.rs:13850-13863).
flaws.refutation: True but materially overstated, and its concrete claim is currently wrong. (1) The harm argument — 'a residual whose stated reason is false is a residual nobody ever re-opens' — is refuted by the rest of the same row, which the finding does not quote: B10's mitigation column already names the correct fix and its status, 'a future durable prepare/commit (persist the assembled signed tx before terminalizing, replay locally) would restore the cooperative path — deliberately not shipped as a half-mechanism'. An implementer reading the row does not conclude the recovery is impossible; they conclude it is unbuilt, which is exactly right. (2) The finding's concrete assertion — 'resending the identical sign/second returns the same partial and the split completes' — is FALSE as the system is specified. The coordinator's sign/second re-runs the terminality gates ahead of the lockbox and returns 410 Gone when `finalized >= budget` (server/src/endpoints/sign.rs:255-299), with no idempotency cache of its own. For the budget-consuming co-signature, which is precisely B10's case, the replay is refused before it can reach the cache. So B10's conclusion happens to be correct today for the case it describes, even though the reason it gives is wrong. That is a smaller defect than 'two normative statements contradict each other, and the false one closes a residual'. (3) The finding correctly keeps the ORDERING half as irreducible; I confirmed the argument (a second co-signature over a terminal node is the INV-19 fork).
flaws.corrected_design_fix: A wording correction plus one normative addition, not a redesign. Delete the 'persisting nonces buys nothing' sentence and record instead: (i) the client never persists a secnonce — only {msg, session, its own partial, the unsigned tx}; (ii) the SE-side session-keyed idempotent re-serve is a normative part of the signing round; (iii) THEREFORE every gate that sits in front of the SE and can refuse a co-signature — the coordinator's single-use, spend-budget, epoch-deadline and pending-transfer checks — MUST be cache-aware, i.e. must serve an already-served session rather than refuse it, exactly as the lockbox's budget check already does. Without (iii) the keystone is defeated at the coordinator and B10's recovery really is unavailable. Keep 'the budget must precede the co-signature' as the boundary with tokens.rs's two-branch argument. Keep the insert_raw_backup_txs DELETE+INSERT atomicity MUST — it is already SPEC-ROADMAP §14(ii).

flaws.title: The sig-count attestation authenticates the wire, not the storage — monotonicity is an undeclared durability requirement, and a rollback is undetectable
flaws.goal_threatened: The conditional part of D28/D8-CLOSE: 'terminality is SE-enforced and SE-attested' holds only if the counter store is fresh. Not covered by B1 (key-share erasure / collusion) or B7 (client-side loss), so it is genuinely unlisted.
flaws.scenario: Reachable, but narrower than stated — see the three mitigations below.
flaws.refutation: The core observation holds and I could not refute it: the digest is assembled host-side from plain SQL reads of `signature_count` and `get_sig_budget` (server.cpp:466-575), `enclave::attest_sig_count` Schnorr-signs a caller-supplied `message32` and holds no counter, no budget and no history (enclave.cpp:299-338), the nonce is documented as anti-replay only, and no participant persists a high-water mark. A3 states monotonicity as behaviour, and no document states a durability or anti-rollback requirement. But three mitigations the finding misses shrink it from high to medium. (a) THE BUDGET IS STORED TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY — the coordinator keeps its own `deposit::get_sig_budget` and its own `count_finalized_signatures` and gates sign/second on them (server/src/endpoints/sign.rs:106-115, :283-299) in addition to the lockbox's. A restore of one store alone does NOT produce the INV-19 fork; both must roll back together. Only the census-hiding half survives a lockbox-only restore. (b) THE CENSUS ALREADY REJECTS AN UNDERCOUNT, not just an overcount (`rejects_undercount`: verify_bundle(&b, 2, 0).is_err()), so any current owner who re-verifies their own bundle detects a rollback below their own disclosed set. The missing piece is only cross-session persistence of the last attested pair — the predicate exists. (c) A ROLLBACK SPANNING ANY TRANSFER IS LOUD, NOT SILENT: keyupdate rotates the coin's server share, so a restore reverts `enclave_public_key` and the aggregate no longer reconstructs the on-chain tx0 output, which `validate_tx0_output_pubkey` catches. Only a window containing co-signatures but no transfers is silent. Separately, the host/enclave framing has little purchase on the shipping deployment: the lockbox is a plain process with no SGX separation, so 'the host builds the digest' is not a boundary crossing there — the operator's storage is the boundary, which is exactly the finding's real point and should be stated that way.
flaws.corrected_design_fix: Adopt (iii); reject (i) and (ii). (iii) is right and cheap: state normatively that the SE's counter and budget store MUST be crash-durable and MUST NEVER be restored to an earlier state; that a restore is a fleet-wide security event requiring re-verification rather than routine recovery; and that a client SHOULD persist the highest attested (count, budget) it has ever seen per sid and refuse any lower one. Add the corollary the finding does not draw: because the budget lives in two independent stores, the spec should REQUIRE that both be consulted and that a disagreement between coordinator and SE counts be treated as a rollback signal — that is free detection the deployment already has and does not use. Reject (ii): a sealed monotone counter does not solve this. Sealing provides confidentiality and integrity, not FRESHNESS — SGX rollback protection is the known-hard case, and in the shipping lockbox deployment there is no enclave separation for a sealed counter to live behind. Reject (i) for now: chained attestations require a publication channel and an append-only log the design does not have, and the corpus has already settled against published state (TRUST-MODEL:119-123, compiled-in constants, against PROTOCOL's nostr claim). Revisit (i) only if a public audit log is adopted for other reasons.

flaws.title: A flat backup may legally carry an RGB transition, and nothing binds its assignment — the sender's hop-backup is an undetectable allocation-theft primitive
flaws.goal_threatened: Allocation integrity on the CTES-R coloured laddered lane, and — the part that actually matters — the corpus's economic-security argument that a prior owner's spend of F is unprofitable griefing
flaws.scenario: Reachable as described on the coloured laddered lane, with corrections. Verified: (1) the coloured whole-coin hop exists (`cosign_colored_receiver_state`, tesr.rs:2059 `build_colored_receiver_state`) and `create_backup_transactions` runs unconditionally after it (transfer_sender.rs:1289) — the honest builder is `new_transaction` (plain, :1427), but a malicious sender is free to substitute a coloured build. (2) The receiver's flat-backup validator does not look: `validate_backup_chain_v2` runs signature / sequence / locktime-shape / reconstruction / INV-5 only, and `verify_if_locktime_is_reasonable_tx_version_and_output_size` (receiver.rs:637-673) admits `op_return_outputs <= 1`. `reconstruct_transaction` (:1031) is a canonical-serialisation check that copies `tx_n.output` verbatim, so it constrains nothing. (3) `verify_colored_shape` (tesr.rs:11344) iterates `bundle.exit_tiers()` only; `accept_colored_ladder` validates against `ladder_txids()` only. A grep for opret inspection outside those two sites returns nothing. So a coloured flat backup passes every receiver check.
flaws.refutation:
Three of the finding's load-bearing claims are wrong, and they change both the fix and the severity.

(a) PROPOSED FIX (b) IS ALREADY IMPLEMENTED, so the legacy half of the finding is refuted. On the un-laddered carrier lane the sender DOES convey the coloured backup's consignment (`rgb_consignment` + `rgb_blinding` on the backup row) and the receiver runs `verify_consignment_assignment(w, &env, &txids, &txid, vout)` where `(txid, vout)` are read from the RECEIVER'S OWN coin record (tokens.rs:5700-5750), then re-checks `received == booked` after `accept_ladder`, with a `PERMANENT-INVALID` sentinel on mismatch. It is explicitly the same predicate the SSP pre-payment gate runs (`validate_pending_token`). "The receiver never sees that consignment at all" is false.

(b) THE INCREMENTAL VICTIM LOSS IS ZERO. INV-5 (`ladder_decrements_by_interval`) makes the current owner's backup the LOWEST locktime in the chain, so the poisoned backup at L_1 can only fire in a window where the same holder is already past their own epoch expiry — the window in which any prior owner's PLAIN backup takes the coin anyway (`epoch_deadline_from_flat_backups`, `check_exit_headroom`). Bob's loss is total in both cases. What changes is the ATTACKER's payoff, from 0 (destruction) to the whole allocation (capture), for ~250 sat, patiently and invisibly. That is why the finding still matters: PROTOCOL.md §5.8's "damage:cost ratio ~0.4 — griefing is economically losing" and the whole mass-grief costing assume the prior owner gains nothing by voiding the tree. On a coloured coin with a coloured backup that assumption is false.

(c) THE SELF-INFLICTED HALF IS ALREADY CLOSED. "if Bob ever uses it, he executes the theft himself" is not reachable: `unilateral_exit` opens for exactly one class — a carrier whose ladder is COLOURED — and drives `tesr::exit_pass` over the tier chain, with a fail-closed refusal at the flat fallback (CTESR-GATE.md §4.1, wallet.rs `colored_ladder_sids`); `refuse_uncolored_over_colored{,_child,_tip}` guard the split/rollover/detrigger lanes and `withdraw`/`refresh` refuse carriers outright. Bob is never routed to his flat backup.

(d) DETECTION EXISTS AFTER THE FACT, on all three lanes: `f_spender` → `WatchState::Void { spender, detail }` (tesr.rs:1299, :9826, :9925) fires when F is spent by anything other than this coin's trigger and carries the spender txid, with a unit test asserting the txid is retained "so the owner can see who took it". It cannot distinguish destruction from capture, which is exactly what fix (a) would make unnecessary.

(e) REACHABILITY CAVEAT: `SdkConfig::colored_ladder` ships **false** (config.rs:357, :388), so no coin is minted into this shape today. This is a spec gap to close before the flag flips, not a live exposure.
flaws.corrected_design_fix:
Keep (a) and (c); drop (b) as already-built.

(a) Make the permitted backup shape a function of the DECLARED LANE rather than the union of two lanes' shapes. On a bundle where `is_colored()`, every flat backup MUST be plain: refuse by name any conveyed backup carrying an OP_RETURN, in the same predicate that already runs on every flat backup, and make that refusal part of the R' acceptance set alongside `verify_colored_shape`. This is one predicate and it fails closed. Note that the permissive `op_return_outputs <= 1` must STAY for the un-laddered carrier lane, where the coloured backup is the transfer vehicle — which is precisely the point: one validator currently serves two lanes with opposite requirements, and the union is the surface.

(c) State the invariant in PROTOCOL.md §5.10: every SE co-signed spend of a coloured coin's funding outpoint F is either (i) plain, and therefore an acknowledged allocation-destroying spend that no exit path may recommend, or (ii) coloured, receiver-assigned, and verified as such by the receiver's own `verify_consignment_assignment`. An unverified opret on a spend of F is a refusal, not a third category.

Also correct the economic text this exposes: PROTOCOL.md §5.8's griefing-is-losing argument and TRUST-MODEL's residual-risk framing are stated for a lane where voiding the tree yields the attacker nothing. Either (a) restores that premise for the coloured lane, or the premise must be restated. Do NOT adopt RGB-2's alternative of colouring every retained rung so a broadcast is a transfer — that generalises this attack rather than closing it.

flaws.title: The coloured lane's economic security is denominated in carrier sats while the loss is denominated in asset value, and the plain flat backup is a BURN rather than a transfer
flaws.goal_threatened: Completeness of the normative economic model for the coloured lane — the payee's exposure, not the attacker's payoff
flaws.scenario: The mechanism is real and already catalogued: the sender's retained 112-vB flat backup over F pays them the whole carrier, costs 6x-265x less than the payee's `293d + 375` vB walk, voids the entire tree in one transaction with zero marginal cost per additional voided piece, and needs no malice. On a coloured tree the voided pieces are not merely stranded — the allocation is closed by an RGB-unaware witness and is destroyed. Every floor in the tree (`min_child_value`, `colored_child_floor`, `colored_spine_tip_floor`, `V_min(d,r)`) is pure fee arithmetic with no asset term.
flaws.refutation:
The mechanism is not new and most of the proposed fix is already the corpus's own scoped work. What survives is one sentence that is genuinely missing.

(a) ALREADY A NORMATIVE, CATALOGUED FINDING. SUBECONOMIC-FINALITY.md is listed in README.md as a normative finding; its own header says "Nothing in this document is built." It states the 112-vB-vs-walk asymmetry, the 6x-265x figure, the zero marginal cost, "It needs no malice", and — decisively — the finding's own fix (a): "Accepting that a piece is a claim, not a bearer instrument — the design choice... what is not defensible is failing to say it." SPEC-ROADMAP.md already carries "Publish V_min(d, r) together with the leaf epoch deadline, or not at all." The sats half is fully covered.

(b) THE STRUCTURAL FIX (c) IS ALREADY THE CORPUS'S CR-D. COLOURED-SPINE-REANCHOR-SCOPE.md §2.3 identifies the on-chain coloured de-trigger re-anchor as buildable-and-unbuilt, ranks it as strictly dominating CR-B, and §5 item 2 explains why nothing short of an on-chain spend of F resets the absolute clock. Worse, (c)'s FIRST alternative — "colour every retained rung so that broadcasting one is a TRANSFER" — is the RGB-1 attack surface generalised, and must be struck.

(c) THE WORKED SCENARIO IS WRONG AS WRITTEN. A coloured in-ladder split leaves the sender's CHANGE allocation on the same tree, so Alice broadcasting her flat backup destroys her own retained 50,000 units alongside Bob's. "Alice's decision was purely a sats decision" holds only when the sender retains no allocation at all. The scenario is repairable, but as stated it is not rational for the actor it describes.

(d) "ABANDONING A COLOURED PIECE DESTROYS AN ASSET" OVERSTATES. Abandonment destroys nothing by itself: the cooperative SE-co-signed exit (~111 vB) and onward transfer both remain, and destruction requires a prior owner to actually spend F. The correct statement is the corpus's own: below V_min the piece is a claim, not a bearer instrument.

(e) G8 IS NOT FALSIFIED. It bounds the ATTACKER'S GAIN, and that gain is correctly sats-denominated — the flat backup recovers the whole carrier including the sats paid away, so it IS a transfer on the sats side. What is uncovered is the VICTIM'S EXPOSURE, which no sats floor bounds. "The attacker gains what the victim loses" was never the design's bound; it is the analyst's paraphrase.

Surviving core, and it is one sentence: nowhere in the corpus is it stated that on the coloured lane an allocation's economic security is bounded by the sats of the carrier it rides and by the sats cost of defending that carrier. SUBECONOMIC-FINALITY.md explicitly waves colour off ("Colour is irrelevant to this finding — the top-up dominates the rung"), which is true of the ARITHMETIC and misleading about the CONSEQUENCE.
flaws.corrected_design_fix:
(a) Add the missing normative statement, and only that, to TRUST-MODEL.md and PROTOCOL.md §5.10: on the coloured lane the economic security of an allocation is bounded by the SATS value of its carrier and by the sats cost of defending it — not by the asset's value — so a carrier must be minted with sats commensurate with what it will carry, and this is a user-visible property of the instrument. Amend SUBECONOMIC-FINALITY.md's "Colour is irrelevant to this finding" to say that it is irrelevant to the arithmetic and load-bearing for the consequence: on the plain lane the voided piece's sats are recovered by the sender; on the coloured lane the allocation is destroyed and nobody acquires it.

(b) Make the asset-aware admission gate a DISCLOSURE, not a refusal. Surface to the payee, before claiming, the sats cost of defending the piece at their own stress fee rate and the fact that the cheapest destruction of the allocation costs the holder of rung L_k about 112 vB. A hard receiver-side refusal keyed on the receiver's fee estimator would refuse honest payments during any spike and would move the payer/payee liveness failure to the worst possible moment; the corpus's own C-2 analysis (the payee cannot fee-bump a tier at all today) shows the refusal would fire constantly.

(c) Reference CR-D (COLOURED-SPINE-REANCHOR-SCOPE §2.3) as the structural remedy rather than proposing a new one, and strike "colour every retained rung" — that is RGB-1's attack, not a fix.
